pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: I’m getting used to the cold
paragraphs: Fictional relocation profile: previously drove most places. Now takes the bus and checks the timetable. Joined a weekly social group. Cold weather and occasional homesickness remain difficult. These are role facts, not a permanent biography for the speakers.

pages.title: A new routine
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: How are you settling in? Is the new routine getting easier?
lines.audioText: How are you settling in? Is the new routine getting easier?
lines.translation: Como está a adaptação? A nova rotina está ficando mais fácil?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Some parts are. I’m used to taking the bus now, but the cold still surprises me
lines.audioText: Some parts are. I’m used to taking the bus now, but the cold still surprises me.
lines.translation: Algumas partes, sim. Já estou acostumada a pegar o ônibus, mas o frio ainda me surpreende

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Did you use to drive everywhere before the move?
lines.audioText: Did you use to drive everywhere before the move?
lines.translation: Você costumava ir a todos os lugares de carro antes da mudança?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I did. At first I missed the last bus twice because I didn’t check the timetable
lines.audioText: I did. At first I missed the last bus twice because I didn’t check the timetable.
lines.translation: Sim. No começo perdi o último ônibus duas vezes porque não olhei os horários

questions.prompt: What is Ana used to doing now?
questions.answer: Ana is used to taking the bus now

questions.prompt: How did she usually travel before moving?
Why did she miss the last bus at first?
questions.answer: Ana missed the last bus because she didn’t check the timetable

pages.title: What has helped?
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What helped you get used to it?
lines.audioText: What helped you get used to it?
lines.translation: O que ajudou você a se acostumar?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Planning the journey before leaving. I’m still getting used to dressing in layers, though
lines.audioText: Planning the journey before leaving. I’m still getting used to dressing in layers, though.
lines.translation: Planejar o trajeto antes de sair. Mas ainda estou me acostumando a vestir várias camadas

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: And have you had time to make friends?
lines.audioText: And have you had time to make friends?
lines.translation: E teve tempo para fazer amigos?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: A little. I’ve joined a weekly group, and that makes the place feel less unfamiliar
lines.audioText: A little. I’ve joined a weekly group, and that makes the place feel less unfamiliar.
lines.translation: Um pouco. Entrei em um grupo semanal e isso faz o lugar parecer menos desconhecido

pages.title: An honest update
pages.instruction: Listen to both voice notes, then answer and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. Taking the bus is much easier now. I’m used to checking the timetable before I leave, so I haven’t missed the last bus again. The cold is still difficult, especially deciding what to wear when the weather changes during the day
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. Taking the bus is much easier now. I’m used to checking the timetable before I leave, so I haven’t missed the last bus again. The cold is still difficult, especially deciding what to wear when the weather changes during the day.
